definitions.gloss: silencing someone; gagging; shutting someone up
definitions.explanation: The act of preventing someone from speaking about something, whether through threats, bribery, or other means. Also refers to the bribe or means used to keep someone quiet.

examples.japanese: {口封|くちふう}じのために{金|かね}を{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: He paid hush money to keep them quiet.

examples.japanese: {証人|しょうにん}を{口封|くちふう}じしようとした{容疑|ようぎ}で{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: He was arrested on suspicion of attempting to silence the witness.

examples.japanese: {不祥事|ふしょうじ}が{明|あき}るみに{出|で}ないように、{関係者|かんけいしゃ}の{口封|くちふう}じが{行|おこな}われていた。
examples.english: Those involved were silenced so that the scandal would not come to light.

notes:
USAGE:
{口封|くちふう}じ literally means "sealing the mouth." It is commonly used with する ({口封|くちふう}じする — to silence someone) and often appears in crime and scandal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口封|くちふう}じする (to silence someone)
- {口封|くちふう}じのために (in order to keep someone quiet)
- {口封|くちふう}じ{料|りょう} (hush money)
- {口封|くちふう}じを{図|はか}る (to attempt to silence someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{口止|くちど}め also means silencing someone or asking them to keep a secret, but {口封|くちふう}じ carries a stronger, more sinister connotation of forceful suppression.
